title: He Taught Me How to Walk
old_p1: Long ago, Heavenly Father spoke through Hosea, a prophet. A prophet tells Heavenly Father’s words. Hosea talked about Israel, Heavenly Father’s family, as if they were a little child.
“When Israel was a child, then I loved him,” He said, “and called my son out of Egypt.” He had led them out of hard work in Egypt. Matthew wrote that these words were about Jesus, too.
old_p2: “I taught Ephraim also to go,” He said, “taking them by their arms.” Ephraim was another name for His people. He held them up the way a dad holds a baby’s hands for wobbly first steps.
They did not even know He was the one healing them. He helped them anyway.
Someone held your hands when you learned to walk. Tonight, feel how Heavenly Father holds you close, too.
p1: Hosea was a prophet. He told how Heavenly Father loves His people, like a parent loves a little child.

Heavenly Father said, “When Israel was a child, I loved him. I called my son out of Egypt.” His people once worked for a mean king in Egypt. He led them out. Matthew later said these words were about Jesus too.
His people wandered away, but He still helped them. He said, “I taught Ephraim to walk, holding them by their arms.” Ephraim is a name for His people.
p2: Think of a baby learning to walk. A parent holds the baby’s arms, so the baby won’t fall. Heavenly Father held His people up like that.
Someone held your hands when you learned to walk. Tonight you can say, “Thank You, Heavenly Father, for holding me up.”
